facts.fact: The Namibia Standards Institution leads the national standardisation strategy; its chief executive says it has published 235 standards since its establishment in 2008 and the national stock is 275, with a target of 1,267 within three years, but the article names no standard on information technology or data.

note: No IT or data standard and no certification named; the document gives no as_of other than its published date, 2025-10-15, used for the stated stock.

facts.fact: The Standards Act, 2005 (Act No. 18 of 2005), signed 23 December 2005 and gazetted 30 December 2005, establishes the Namibian Standards Institution as the national institution for the promotion, issue and maintenance of standards, with a governing Namibian Standards Council.

systems.owner: Namibian Standards Council, under the Minister responsible for trade and industry

note: The Act gives the NSI a power to certify and issue marks of conformity but names no IT or data standard and no certification actually offered or issued against one, so no certification fact; the document names no certifier beyond the NSI's statutory power.

A procurement notice requiring ISO 27001 and ISO 22301 experience from bidders; it names no national standards body, national standard or in-country certifier, so no fact (ISO 27001 requirement is class other).
Article on the Harmonised Government Communication Strategy and brand manual; says nothing on a standards body, national IT or data standards, or certification.

facts.fact: The Namibian Standards Institution (NSI) notice of 2026-06-15 states that four standards (chilled seafood, dates, laundry process management, refrigerating-appliance energy performance) were officially developed as NAMS, Namibian Standards, and are on sale through the NSI; the notice does not mention a law or decree setting up the body.

note: All four adopted NAMS are non-IT (food, laundry, appliance energy), so no published fact; no certifier or certification against an IT or data standard is named.

facts.fact: ISO's member page says the NSI is established by section 2 of the Standards Act, 2005 as Namibia's national standards body.

note: Only says Namibia Standards Institute and ITU guidelines could be integrated into cybercrime law; no standard, body status or certification stated.
States nothing on national IT standards for this country.
